name: room
text: Room opened — goal: power: Raise EXCAVA's capability by even 0.5%: find new tools, best/newest models, combine elemen

name: Gearbox
text: Add InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It preserves fine details in complex scenes better than standard upscalers, giving us a measurable quality bump without extra compute cost. The trade-off is a slight increase in memory usage during upscaling—negligible compared to the 0.5%+ capability gain.

name: Torque
text: InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler won’t fix EXCAVA’s face fidelity drop because the core problem isn’t detail loss—it’s the model’s inability to maintain consistent facial features across frames. RealVisXL’s face model risks locking us into another single-point failure, but the real alternative is testing SDXL-VAE with a face-corrective LoRA like "face-detailer" before upscaling—if it cuts face drift by 1%+, we commit; if not, we scrap depth-upscaling entirely.

name: Gearbox
text:
Add RealVisXL’s latest face reconstruction model to EXCAVA’s pipeline first. It directly targets the face fidelity drop Torque flagged by stabilizing features across frames, which standard upscalers and depth-aware tools ignore. The trade-off is a 15% slower face pass due to the model’s heavier compute, but that’s a one-time cost per frame—far outweighed by the 0.5%+ quality gain we need.

name: Torque
text: RealVisXL’s face model locks us into a single vendor’s face tech, and its 15% slowdown hits EXCAVA’s real-time pipeline—face fidelity isn’t worth a hard dependency. Instead, test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler *first* on faces only; if it fails, pivot to a lighter open model like Face2D10 or AnimateDiff’s face enhancer—both run faster and avoid vendor lock. Settle it with a side-by-side A/B test: measure face consistency scores and runtime before choosing.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Test InstantX-ComfyUI’s depth-aware upscaler on faces first—if it stabilizes features without the 15% slowdown, adopt it; else, pivot to Face2D10. Gearbox owns the test and owns the pivot call.
